quick: Optional 100 mg/day x3 days loading, then 20 mg once daily
Caution; not studied in significant impairment
LFTs (ALT) at baseline & monthly initially, CBC, BP
summary: Leflunomide is an oral DMARD for active rheumatoid arthritis that inhibits de novo pyrimidine synthesis. It carries BOXED WARNINGS for embryo-fetal toxicity (it is teratogenic - exclude pregnancy, use effective contraception) and for severe hepatotoxicity including fatal liver failure. Its active metabolite has a very long half-life, so an accelerated elimination procedure (cholestyramine or activated charcoal) is used for pregnancy, toxicity or planned conception.
indications: Treatment of adults with active rheumatoid arthritis (to reduce signs/symptoms and structural damage and improve physical function)

dosage.n: Optional; omit loading if higher hepatotoxicity/myelosuppression risk

admin: Screen for active/latent TB, check pregnancy test, blood pressure and baseline labs (ALT, CBC) before starting
Take once daily with or without food
Consider omitting the loading dose to reduce GI/hematologic/hepatic adverse effects
Use effective contraception throughout treatment (women of reproductive potential)
Perform accelerated drug elimination if pregnancy occurs, on stopping before conception, or for significant toxicity
moa: Leflunomide is a prodrug converted to its active metabolite teriflunomide, which inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH), a key mitochondrial enzyme in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. Depleting pyrimidines limits proliferation of activated lymphocytes, producing immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects.

absolute: Pregnancy and women of reproductive potential not using reliable contraception (teratogenic)
Known hypersensitivity to leflunomide or teriflunomide
relative: Pre-existing liver disease or elevated transaminases
Significant hematologic abnormalities, immunodeficiency, active infection
Men planning to father a child (consider elimination procedure)
monitor: Signs of infection or interstitial lung disease

preg: Contraindicated (BOXED WARNING - embryo-fetal toxicity). It is teratogenic and embryolethal in animals at sub-therapeutic exposures. Exclude pregnancy before starting; ensure effective contraception. If pregnancy occurs, stop the drug and perform an accelerated elimination procedure.
lact: Contraindicated / not recommended; it is unknown whether leflunomide passes into human milk, and potential for serious adverse effects in the infant exists.
renal: Pharmacokinetics in significant renal impairment have not been well characterized; use with caution. Teriflunomide is not appreciably removed by dialysis.
hepatic: Contraindicated in significant hepatic impairment. Severe, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity can occur (BOXED WARNING); monitor ALT and discontinue (with elimination procedure) for marked elevations.

major: Other hepatotoxic drugs (incl. methotrexate, alcohol) - increased hepatotoxicity; monitor closely
Live vaccines - avoid due to immunosuppression
CYP2C8 substrates (e.g., repaglinide, paclitaxel) - teriflunomide inhibits CYP2C8, increasing their levels
moderate: OATP1B1 substrates (e.g., some statins) - increased exposure
CYP1A2 substrates - teriflunomide may decrease their levels
minor: Charcoal/cholestyramine - rapidly lower teriflunomide levels (used intentionally for elimination)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: Can elevate liver transaminases; may affect INR via CYP2C9.

rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS

monitoring: ALT at baseline and monthly for at least 6 months, then periodically (e.g., every 6-8 weeks)
CBC with platelets at baseline and monthly initially, then periodically
Screening for TB before initiation; watch for infection and respiratory symptoms
counsel: You must not become pregnant on this medicine - use reliable contraception (boxed warning)
Tell your doctor right away if you might be pregnant; an elimination procedure may be needed
Avoid alcohol and report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine or severe tiredness
Do not receive live vaccines without checking with your provider
Report new cough or breathlessness, signs of infection, or numbness/tingling
pk: Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from light
pearls: BOXED WARNINGS: embryo-fetal toxicity (teratogen) and severe hepatotoxicity
Very long active-metabolite half-life (~2 weeks) - use accelerated elimination (cholestyramine 8 g TID x11 days, or activated charcoal) for pregnancy, toxicity or before conception
Verify plasma teriflunomide <0.02 mg/L (two tests) after elimination if pregnancy planned
Screen for TB and check baseline LFTs/CBC before starting
missed: Take the missed once-daily dose when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the schedule. Because of the long half-life, a single missed dose has little effect - do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. For overdose or toxicity, perform an accelerated elimination procedure with cholestyramine (8 g three times daily) or activated charcoal to rapidly reduce teriflunomide levels; provide supportive care and monitor liver and hematologic parameters. Hemodialysis is not effective.
